newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors to question former deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors to question former deputy PM.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors summoned former deputy prime minister Rha Woong-bae for questioning in connection with a loans-for-kickback scandal involving the troubled Hanbo Group, a prosecution official said on Thursday.
"Prosecutors asked Rha Woong-bae to appear at the prosecution office on Friday morning," said the official who asked not to be identified.
Rha served as deputy prime minister in charge of the finance and economy ministry from December 1995 to August 1996.
State prosecutors have been probing politicians who allegedly received money from Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo. Government officials said 33 politicians have been pointed out by Chung.

The inquiry started last week and so far more than half of the politicians have been questioned. Most of them confessed to taking political contibutions from Chung but deny returning any favours. The National Assembly speaker will also be questioned soon.
